Settled as option (a): the criterion 'Failed-importer tests are added to an otherwise ordinary answer' was a leak from so-n6b.2 and has been struck from so-jr5.2. jr5.2 ships the blunt whole-graph refusal on any non-zero resolution_errors, as its own description states; so-n6b.2 (depending on so-n6b.5 for failed_importers) later replaces that refusal with the localised always-run set. Existing dependency edges are correct and unchanged. Verified against the code: failed_importers exists nowhere in the repo, so jr5.2 could not have implemented the localised rule today.

Settled as option (b) by the epic owner. The expired-profile blind spot STAYS in so-jr5.2, and downwind_of grows a third input:

  downwind_of(maps, changed_files, existing_files) -> DownwindResult

existing_files is the set of files that exist in the working tree now, enumerated by so-jr5.4 and passed in as plain data, so the rules stay pure and IO-free and DownwindMaps stays free of the filesystem. Expiry is 'any(not maps.knows(p) for p in existing_files)' -- so-n6b.1's divergence definition read straight off the maps' public surface.

DECIDING REASON: expiry and the unknown-changed-path rule overlap. A file you add yourself is both a changed path the maps have never seen and the file that expires the profile -- one answer, two candidate reasons, and per so-jr5.4 the reason is the whole product when the tool declines to select. Under option (a) the short-circuit in jr5.4 would always win, the unknown-path rule could never fire in that case, and jr5.2's unit tests would keep passing because they exercise downwind_of in isolation and never see the short-circuit above them. That is exactly the 'rule that quietly wins over another' jr5.2's description exists to prevent, made harder to catch by crossing a component boundary no single test observes. It also keeps expiry consistent with resolution_errors, already a whole-profile blind spot that so-n6b.8 deliberately placed inside jr5.2 rather than in the caller.

The cost was real and accepted: it reverses so-n6b.8 on the signature, and existing_files is the one input not derived from the profile, carrying a scoping policy likely to churn (so-746, monorepo roots).

Settled by the epic owner. The set of files compared against the maps is scoped, and the scope is RECORDED IN THE PROFILE AT CAPTURE TIME.

THE SCOPE is the coverage targets union the pytest test paths, as actually resolved by the profiling run, written into ProfilingData alongside so-746's repo root. IN SCOPE means a .py file under those roots, enumerated by plain 'git ls-files' -- tracked files only. On this repository the roots are {smoke_optimiser, tests}, putting 38 files in scope and leaving out scripts/branch_summary.py, smoke_optimiser/py.typed and the 13 tracked root files.

WHY RECORDED RATHER THAN RECOMPUTED: config.cov_source is not reliably what was measured. runner.py:290-298 appends --cov={cov_source} only when config.pytest_args lacks a --cov, and never inspects the project's own addopts -- this repository's pyproject.toml:67 already carries --cov=smoke_optimiser. Recomputing from config therefore lets 'known to the maps' and 'in scope for expiry' drift apart, which is the exact failure this issue names. Recording makes the check unable to disagree with the run that produced the maps, and so-746 already sets the precedent for capture-time facts living in the profile.

WHY TEST PATHS ARE IN SCOPE: tests/*.py are absent from measured_files under --cov=smoke_optimiser and reach knows() only via ImportGraph.unattributed_modules. Scoping to the coverage targets alone would leave a teammate's new tests/test_discounts.py invisible, so the maps would answer confidently and wrongly for an edited rates.py -- so-n6b.1's own motivating scenario, silently under-selected. The cost is accepted: every new test file costs one instrumented full run, which so-n6b.7 prices and so-n6b.17 may reduce.

WHY TRACKED ONLY: an untracked file is one you just created, and so-7hr already places it in the changed set, where so-jr5.2's unknown-changed-path rule answers it and names the accurate reason. Including untracked files in existing_files would give such a file two candidate reasons and buy nothing, since both routes reach a full suite. Tracked-only leaves expiry's domain as files that arrived by pull or checkout -- the only case no other rule sees -- and makes the two domains disjoint by construction. Relying on .gitignore also makes a scope root of '.' survivable, which config.py's _discover_cov_target can produce.

CONFIG DRIFT EXPIRES, on any difference between the recorded roots and the ones the current configuration resolves to. Without it, widening --cov would silently never expire anything and the newly-in-scope tree would stay invisible though a regenerated profile would know it. On resolved roots, never on configuration text.

A PROFILE WITH NO RECORDED SCOPE IS A HARD ERROR naming the fix, not a silent full-suite run. This is a 0.x library and a profile is a cache one instrumented run rebuilds, so users reprofile on upgrade rather than being migrated.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED, do not re-propose:
• Recompute the scope from configuration at check time. Rejected above: cov_source is not the measured scope, and the drift is silent.
• Derive the scope from the directory roots of measured_files. Self-consistent, no new field -- but it defines 'in scope' as 'where the profile already has files', which makes the criterion 'a file in scope is one a regenerated profile would know' near-tautological. Under the natural reading (every directory containing a known file) any new subpackage is invisible, and the hole is permanent rather than a one-off cost. It also cannot express the config-drift check at all, having no recorded scope to compare.
• Filesystem walk instead of git. Needs hand-rolled ignore rules for .venv, __pycache__ and egg-info -- a second definition of 'project file' that drifts from .gitignore.
• Staged files only. Not coherent for an existence question: staging says what is in your commit, not what is on disk and collectable by pytest.

KNOWN HOLE, accepted: source that is gitignored (generated protobuf stubs and the like) never expires a profile. It becomes known once a profiling run measures it.

That is real, and it is so-n6b.18 rather than part of the MVP, because deciding it requires knowing the scope the NEXT run would measure -- which smoke-optimiser cannot currently determine, for the same reason recomputation was rejected above. A naive 'recorded != currently resolved' comparison is TRUE ON EVERY RUN wherever the project's addopts carry a --cov that differs from what _discover_cov_target returns, pinning the profile to expired forever: the born-expired failure this issue exists to eliminate, reintroduced through the comparison meant to strengthen it. ProfilingDataFile now carries a required, non-defaulted schema_version field (PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION=1). load_profiling_data_file checks it before Pydantic validation runs and raises ProfileSchemaMismatchError, which cli.py reports with a distinct message naming both versions and telling the user to reprofile -- separate from the generic 'failed to parse' message used for genuine corruption. The old 'recorded by an older version' guess is removed from the generic message. Noted in CHANGELOG.md as a breaking change. Tests cover both error paths in tests/test_profiler_models.py and tests/test_cli.py.

Implemented in smoke_optimiser/reports/downwind_suite.py: DownwindSuiteFile (own version, changed_files, node_ids, profile identity as commit+timestamp, blind_spots) plus write/read helpers, and wired --downwind/--downwind-file-path into plugin.py with its own filtering, missing-test warning wording, and a coverage-free report header. Confirmed with the user: blind_spots is a list of {reason, file, resolution_errors} entries (not a single reason) since jr5.2 documents multiple independent rules firing per changed file; BlindSpotReason enum values are fixed now (unknown_path, non_python_file, unattributed_import, expired_profile, changed_conftest, resolution_errors) rather than left as free text; node_ids is left empty when blind_spots is non-empty because the only reader is the plugin, whose fallback behaviour is 'don't filter' -- pytest already collects everything for free, so enumerating every id would add nothing for either the plugin or a human reading the file. .smoke_suite.json and the coverage-per-second path are untouched.

Implemented changed_files(repo_root) in smoke_optimiser/downwind/changes.py, parsing git status --porcelain=v2 -z (staged+unstaged+untracked union, -M renames resolved to old path, deletions never filtered). Design decisions confirmed with user: repo_root is a caller-supplied parameter (not self-discovered), missing/failed git raises GitStatusError, and edge statuses (merge conflicts, type changes) classify as MODIFIED. 15 new tests in tests/test_downwind_changes.py against real temp git repos; 95% branch coverage on the new module.

Two signals now guard the profiling run, because the exit code alone cannot carry it.

The inline profiling hook grows a pytest_collectreport hook that records every node id pytest failed to collect, merged across xdist workers through the outcomes file (OutcomesFileModel gains a required collection_errors list). Any collection error is fatal however many iterations have already run: the same files fail to collect every time, so accumulated coverage never makes up for tests that were never collected. This is what closes the hole the issue was aimed at -- --continue-on-collection-errors makes a collection error exit 1, indistinguishable from ordinary test failures, and a project can set it in its own addopts where no flag smoke-optimiser sees ever mentions it.

The exit code is then checked against pytest.ExitCode: OK and TESTS_FAILED proceed, everything else (plus codes pytest does not define, e.g. a signal) is fatal, each with its own message -- NO_TESTS_COLLECTED now says so instead of falling through to a missing-database CoverageIngestError.

Decision on --iterations > 1: an abandoned iteration stops the loop but keeps what completed. Coverage accumulates into one database, so the earlier iterations' work is intact; the abandoned iteration's outcomes and import graph are dropped whole, since tests it never reached would be averaged over fewer samples than the rest. If the first iteration is the one that fails there is nothing to keep, and the run fails.

Tests: three e2e runs over a project with one uncollectable test file (default exit 2, --continue-on-collection-errors exit 1, and a plain failing test that must still profile), plus unit coverage of each fatal exit code, the mid-run abandonment, and the hook recording collection errors.

Fixed by making boolean CLI flags tri-state: 'bool | None = None' with paired --x/--no-x forms, chosen over the 'flag or None' shape so-u3i used. The issue offered that alternative, but it only fixes precedence in one direction -- a pyproject 'allow_ordered = true' would have become impossible to turn off from the command line. The rule this establishes for so-jr5.4: the CLI wins over pyproject.toml both ways, and 'not passed' is None. Also emits both halves in reports/repro.py, and widened the --help scrape in test_repro_command_completeness_against_help, which the longer paired flag name made wrap and truncate.
Added pydantic model_validators to BlindSpotModel (reason/file/resolution_errors consistency) and DownwindSuiteFile (node_ids/blind_spots mutual exclusivity); added tests covering each violation.

Decided: the combination is refused. pytest_configure now exits with a clear error naming both flags and why they conflict, placed above the two loaders so the failure is about the flags rather than whichever selection file happens to be missing. Covered by tests/test_plugin.py::test_plugin_smoke_and_downwind_together_is_refused, which passes a missing smoke path alongside a valid downwind file to pin the guard's position. Full design rationale recorded in the issue's design field.

Already satisfied. so-n6b.1's acceptance criteria no longer contain 'Timezone-aware comparison wherever capture time is read'; they were rewritten to the divergence test and end at 'An expired profile takes the full-suite path with expiry named as the reason.' No datetime comparison remains for an implementer to mistake for a definition of done.

The criteria do still say 'the scope roots recorded in the profile at capture time'. Read literally against this issue's acceptance wording that is a reference to capture time, but it is a scope reference -- which roots, as recorded when the profile was captured -- not a datetime comparison, and it is load-bearing for so-n6b.14. Confirmed as satisfying rather than violating the intent.

Closing this unblocks so-n6b.1, and through it the so-jr5.2 -> so-jr5.4 chain, which was the entire reason no P1 MVP work read as ready.

Delivered as the capture-time half of expiry: the profile now records what it measured,
and a pure predicate says which files that covers. The expiry test itself is one line
over that predicate and stays in so-jr5.2, with so-jr5.4 enumerating the tree -- the
issue's acceptance criteria were rewritten to that boundary, since as originally written
they described end-to-end behaviour this issue blocks rather than contains.

WHAT LANDED
* smoke_optimiser/profiler/scope.py: ProfileScope (coverage_roots, test_roots,
  test_file_patterns), resolve_scope() and files_in_scope().
* The scope is resolved INSIDE the profiled pytest process, in the injected hook, from
  pytest-cov's resolved cov_source, pytest's own config.args and config.getini
  ('python_files'). Nothing outside that process can see a project's addopts or
  testpaths, so nothing outside it can state the scope without risking disagreement with
  the run that produced the maps. Coverage sources resolve as coverage.py resolves them:
  path first, then importable name (a src layout needs this), dropped if they land
  outside the repository, kept verbatim if unresolvable rather than failing a finished
  instrumented run.
* PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1 -> 2 with a required 'scope' field, so a version 1 profile is
  refused as a mismatch. A version 2 profile whose scope names nothing raises
  ProfileScopeMissingError, reported by the CLI with its own message naming both the
  command and the settings to check -- reprofiling alone would not fix that case.
* A capture-time warning, with numbered steps, when the resolved test root is the
  repository root.
* CHANGELOG breaking-change entry; PRD section 5.3 documents the field and the rule.

WHY THE SCOPE IS TWO KINDS OF ROOT RATHER THAN ONE FLAT SET, refining so-n6b.14's flat
rule: a project that configures no testpaths leaves pytest pointed at the repository
root, so under the flat rule every stray tracked .py -- a manual script, a vendored
suite, an example -- is in scope, unknowable however often the profile is regenerated,
and the profile is born expired. Narrowing every test root by pytest's collection
patterns fixes that but drops test support modules (tests/helpers/factories.py) under a
precise root, which a regenerated profile WOULD know, and that under-selects silently.
Coverage roots therefore keep the flat rule, precise test roots keep the flat rule, and
only a test root of the repository root -- where location carries no information at all
-- narrows to what pytest would collect. The narrowing is what the new warning tells
users how to get out of.

VALIDATION: ruff check, ruff format, ty check, 199 tests pass. The end-to-end test
profiles a fixture git repository, regenerates, and asserts not-expired both times over
files_in_scope('git ls-files') -- which also confirms empirically that coverage records
files it never executed, so a measured-but-never-imported module is known rather than
divergent.
